title: Culture and assertiveness
content: What counts as 'assertive' isn't culturally universal. Much of the popular assertiveness framework was developed in individualist Western contexts, where direct self-expression is generally valued. In many other cultural contexts, including many Arab, East Asian, and other collectivist cultures, indirectness, deference to elders, and prioritizing group harmony can be the more respected and effective way to communicate a need, not a failure to be assertive. Being assertive doesn't have to mean being blunt or direct in the Western sense, it just means finding a way, within your own context, to express what you need clearly enough that it's actually heard, while staying true to the values and relationships that matter to you.
